To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AMPA receptors on septal neurons are inhibited by acute and chronic ethanol exposure, and this is consistent with ethanol‐induced inhibition of AMPA receptors on other neurons in brain.
AMPA‐activated ion currents in medial septum neurons were directly and selectively inhibited by ethanol, and this inhibition was not altered by ethanol tolerance or dependence.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ethanol on native AMPA receptors in neurons from the medial septum/dia­gnol band (MS/Db) region of the rat brain.
the effects of ethanol and ethanol dependence on the function of glutamatergic synapses in brain areas that are critical for the control of ethanol consumption and withdrawal.
identifying the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the acute and chronic actions of ethanol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AMPA receptors in MS/DB cells are not desensitized to the inhibitory effects of acute ethanol exposure.
ethanol inhibition of native non‐NMDARs on MS/DB is not affected by ethanol tolerance or dependence.
the ethanol‐induced inhibition of native AMPARs is sustained in MS/DB, but not CA1 hippocampal pyramidal, neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethanol inhibits native AMPA receptors in a concentration‐dependent and sustained manner, but does not induce functional tolerance to ethanol inhibition.
ethanol‐induced inhibition of AMPA receptors on the MS/DB neurons is not altered by either ethanol functional tolerance or physical dependence.
ethanol inhibits AMPA receptor function on MS/DB, but not NMDA receptor function on CA1 pyramidal, neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPA‐type receptors are sensitive to ethanol inhibition, but that this sensitivity does not change with ethanol dependence.
the ethanol inhibition of native glutamate receptors on MS/ DB neurons does not undergo adaptation with repeated ethanol exposure sufficient to produce physical dependence.
ethanol inhibition of native non‐NMDARs in the MS/DB is not altered during ethanol dependence.
